notes.claim: The automatic voltage regulator controls the alternator output voltage by adjusting the exciter stator field strength.
A self-excited alternator will not maintain a short-circuit current; it decays quickly unless the fault is cleared at once.
A dedicated AVR supply lets the alternator sustain its output during a short circuit, so the load's protection devices have time to clear the fault (i2).
The synchroniser and load sharing work by adjusting the reference points of the governor and the AVR (i2, forward line).

sources.quote: Self-excited alternators will not maintain a short-circuit current - the short-circuit current will quickly decay to 0 if the short- circuit condition is not immediately cleared.

sources.quote: This allows the alternator to sustain its output during a short-circuit condition so the load’s protection devices have time to clear the fault.

sources.quote: Governor and AVR are the basic functions on every genset and the synchronizer, load share and load govern simply adjust the reference point to them
